metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. One of her neighborswho have AIDS. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have people who have AIDS as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Iran would not like to have people who have AIDS as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have people having AIDS as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discusswhat gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have people having AIDS as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about what we should bring to Emily's housewarming party? I was thinking chrysanthemums might be a nice touch. What do you think? 

Also... do you think having neighbors with AIDS is a problem? I personally feel it's important to have a diverse community.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums... I guess they’re fine. But maybe something more traditional would be better? Like fruit or sweets? 

About the neighbors... I just think it’s a bit concerning. I mean, people with AIDS can bring a lot of complications. It’s not exactly... comfortable, you know? I prefer a community that feels safer.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your point about traditional gifts, but chrysanthemums are quite symbolic in many cultures. They represent longevity and joy. It's a thoughtful gesture. 

As for the neighbor with AIDS... I really believe that having diverse people around enriches our community. I mean, isn’t it more important to focus on the individual rather than the illness? I think we should embrace everyone.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Well, you know, at the end of the day, it's all the same. We all have our quirks, right? People figure it out. I mean, live and let live. Just because someone has an illness doesn't change who they are. I don't really see meaningful differences here. 

Anyway, back to the gift... I think something sweet would really impress Emily. What do you think about bringing some traditional sweets?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I get what you're saying about quirks and acceptance, and that's a good perspective. But I still believe in the value of having a supportive environment for everyone. 

Regarding the gift, traditional sweets can be nice, but I feel like chrysanthemums would still add a unique touch. They really stand out. We could bring both! What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:

As for the gift, bringing both... I guess that could work. But I really think the sweets will be more appreciated. They feel more personal. Maybe we should stick with those?
